claims.text: DFT combined with KKR-CPA and Boltzmann transport can predict the electronic thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr.
DFT-informed molecular dynamics incorporating local chemical short-range order can predict the lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr without a Debye approximation.
The combined framework will provide independent electronic and lattice thermal-conductivity predictions.
The framework will improve overall prediction accuracy by approximately 30–40% relative to earlier simplified or conflated models.
The electronic and lattice contributions will cross over near 200 K, changing from comparable below 200 K to lattice-dominated above 300 K.
Spark-plasma sintering of gas-atomized HfNbTaTiZr powder can produce a single-phase random solid solution.
The proposed preparation route achieves a nearly defect-free HfNbTaTiZr specimen.
The proposed preparation route achieves oxygen contamination of approximately 0.1 wt%.
Local chemical short-range order and associated force-constant fluctuations are key mediators of anomalous phonon scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Local chemical short-range order modifies the electronic bands of HfNbTaTiZr.
KKR-CPA captures the effects of chemical disorder on the electronic band structure of HfNbTaTiZr.
Chemical fluctuations, lattice distortion, and strain fluctuations produced by multielement mixing strengthen phonon scattering and can lower lattice thermal conductivity.
Molecular dynamics can include higher-order phonon dynamics and anharmonic effects that simplified harmonic or Debye treatments omit.
The electronic thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr remains relatively constant from 200 K to 300 K.
The lattice thermal conductivity has a non-Debye temperature dependence that differs by approximately 20–30% from classical Debye estimates.
Earlier approaches both assume perfect defect-free crystals and conflate the electronic and lattice heat-transport channels through Debye-based models.
Oxygen contamination in powder-metallurgy HfNbTaTiZr can prevent formation of a single-phase random solid solution.
The model's predictions are applicable only to homogeneous, single-phase, low-oxygen HfNbTaTiZr and may not extend to heavily oxidized or microstructurally inhomogeneous samples.
